statement: Given that $\\int_{0}^{1}x^{a-1}\,dx=\\frac{1}{a}$ for $a>0$, differentiate both sides with respect to $a$ to evaluate $\\int_{0}^{1}x^{a-1}\\ln x\,dx$.
solution: Differentiating $\\int_{0}^{1}x^{a-1}\,dx=\\frac{1}{a}$ with respect to $a$ (passing the derivative inside the integral) gives $\\int_{0}^{1}\\frac{\\partial}{\\partial a}\bigl(x^{a-1}\bigr)\,dx=\\int_{0}^{1}x^{a-1}\\ln x\,dx$ on the left, and $-\\frac{1}{a^{2}}$ on the right. Therefore $\\int_{0}^{1}x^{a-1}\\ln x\,dx=-\\frac{1}{a^{2}}$ for $a>0$.
hints: Differentiate the integrand x^(a-1) with respect to a.
